2026-08-04T13:00:02.7838271Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7838643Z 
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7838963Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7839431Z 
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7839817Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7840298Z 
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7841831Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7843745Z >
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7845983Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7848345Z >
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7849115Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7849851Z 
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7850024Z ### How to Use
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7850249Z 
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7851007Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7851699Z 
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7851871Z ```bash
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7852392Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7853333Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7853931Z ```
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7854133Z 
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7854389Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7854903Z ```bash
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7855425Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7856209Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7857038Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7857764Z ```
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7857962Z 
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7858570Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7859408Z ```bash
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7860059Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7860729Z ```
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7860927Z 
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7861245Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7861950Z ```bash
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7862466Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7863509Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7864206Z ```
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7864412Z 
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7864664Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7865081Z 
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7866464Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7867989Z 
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7868159Z ```bash
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7868591Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7869418Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7870206Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7870941Z 
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7877524Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7878576Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7879375Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7879827Z ```
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7880028Z 
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7880765Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7881649Z 
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7881819Z ```bash
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7882495Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7883601Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7884304Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7884768Z 
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7885166Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7885952Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7886488Z ```
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7886690Z 
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7886893Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7887693Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7888664Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7889617Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7890606Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7891829Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7892350Z 
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7892520Z ### Notes
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7892925Z 
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7893550Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7894926Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7896167Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7897400Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7898580Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7899680Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7900637Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-08-04T13:00:02.7901324Z </mcp-clis>
